title: Perseverance
definition: Perseverance is continuing in faith, obedience, and hope through trials because God preserves His people in Christ.
summary: Perseverance is continuing in faith, obedience, and hope through trials because God preserves His people in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus endured suffering faithfully, keeps His people by grace, and strengthens them by the Spirit to continue until the end.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Perseverance does not mean believers are strong in themselves. It means God sustains His people through faith, trials, weakness, correction, and growth until He completes His work.

Scripture calls believers to endure, run, watch, pray, and continue in faith. These commands are real, yet they rest on the grace of God who keeps His people in Christ.

Jesus is the faithful One who endured the cross and now strengthens His people. Believers persevere by looking to Him, not by pretending hardship is easy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People in recovery, disability, grief, or long hardship may wonder if they can keep going. Perseverance gives hope that endurance is not self-powered; Christ sustains His people one faithful step at a time.

This doctrine also corrects shallow spirituality that expects instant victory. God often forms faith through long obedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Keep your eyes on Christ in hardship. Use the means God gives—Scripture, prayer, fellowship, repentance, and help from others—and ask the Spirit for strength to take the next faithful step.
